title: Jangoo, Forde and Mangru Earn Maiden West Indies Central Contracts
excerpt: Cricket West Indies handed retainers to 15 men and 15 women for 2026-27, with John Campbell back for the first time since 2019 and every deal tied to a qualification target.
body:
• Cricket West Indies announced 2026-27 retainer contracts on Thursday: 15 senior men, 15 senior women and three men's development deals, running October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027.
  • Matthew Forde, Amir Jangoo and Mandy Mangru earn their first international retainer contracts.
  • Opener John Campbell returns to a central contract for the first time since 2019 after a century against India in Delhi and a 68-ball ODI hundred in Guwahati.
  • The men's first assignment under the new deals is February's ICC Cricket World Cup Qualifier; the women face Pakistan in December with automatic World Cup qualification on the line.

Amir Jangoo, Matthew Forde and Mandy Mangru have earned their first West Indies central contracts, and opener John Campbell has won his place back after seven years, as Cricket West Indies released its retainer lists for the 2026-27 season on Thursday. Fifteen senior men and fifteen senior women received contracts, alongside development deals for three men, the ICC reported. All contracts run from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027.

The three captains remain at the core of the contracted groups: Shai Hope leads the ODI and T20I sides, Roston Chase the Test team, and Hayley Matthews the senior women.

Why the Three New Names Earned Their Deals

Forde was West Indies' leading powerplay wicket-taker across both white-ball formats over the past year, claiming 10 wickets in T20Is and six in ODIs. Jangoo's case was built in Test cricket: a career-best 233 against Sri Lanka in Antigua in June, in a 401-run partnership with Chase that set a world record for the sixth wicket in Tests. He was at it again on the day the contracts were announced, reaching an unbeaten 111 at the end of day one of the second Test against Bangladesh in Sylhet. Mangru, a wicketkeeper-batter who has played six ODIs and 13 T20Is, was part of the squad that reached the semi-finals of the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup.

Campbell's return completes a long road back. The opener registered his maiden Test century with 115 against India in Delhi in October last year, then returned to the ODI side after six years and marked the occasion with a 68-ball 101 in Guwahati in September.

"Every one of these contracts is tied to a job in front of us. For the men, the first job is the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier in February, and we go there with every intention of making it through. Matthew, Amir and Mandy have earned their places in that work, and John has earned his way back."

— Miles Bascombe, CWI Director of Cricket

The Full Lists

Senior men: John Campbell, Keacy Carty, Roston Chase (Test captain), Matthew Forde, Justin Greaves, Shai Hope (ODI and T20I captain), Akeal Hosein, Amir Jangoo, Alzarri Joseph, Shamar Joseph, Gudakesh Motie, Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford, Jayden Seales, Jomel Warrican.

Senior women: Aaliyah Alleyne, Shemaine Campbelle, Jahzara Claxton, Deandra Dottin, Afy Fletcher, Jannillea Glasgow, Realeanna Grimmond, Shawnisha Hector, Chinelle Henry, Zaida James, Mandy Mangru, Hayley Matthews (captain), Ashmini Munisar, Karishma Ramharack, Stafanie Taylor.

Men's development contracts: Jewel Andrew, Ackeem Auguste and Vitel Lawes — all three have already represented West Indies, with Auguste and Lawes receiving their first international contracts. Keacy Carty, Chase, Greaves and Jomel Warrican enter the final year of two-year deals on the men's side, as do Deandra Dottin and Chinelle Henry among the women. CWI clarified that players without central contracts remain eligible for selection, according to Cricbuzz.

What the Contracts Are Aimed At

CWI director of cricket Miles Bascombe framed the list around two assignments. For the men, it is February's World Cup Qualifier, a tournament West Indies cannot afford to fail after missing recent global events. For the women, the three-match ODI series against Pakistan in December, under interim head coach Andre Coley, offers the chance to secure automatic qualification for the next ICC Women's Cricket World Cup. The immediate focus, though, stays in Sylhet, where Bangladesh are hosting West Indies and Jangoo's unbeaten century has already given the selectors a first return on their newest contract.
